_note: Corrective templates, one per check id. `snippet` is a copy-paste fix; null where pasting markup cannot fix the problem (a 500 response, a client-rendered architecture). `validation` is never null — every finding must tell the reader how to confirm the fix worked. PLAN.md §12 places these in the skill's own references so remediation-advisor stays self-contained and independently runnable, which is the padding test it has to pass. The registry's prose `remediation` line remains the action SUMMARY and is not duplicated here. `target` is the file-or-element location hint PLAN.md §7 asks for. It is always present, because roughly half of all findings are an ABSENCE with no element to point at — a missing meta tag has no selector, and "add it in <head>" is the only address that exists. The analyzer's `selector` remains the precise element when there is one; the two are complementary, not alternatives.

_placeholders.{{SITE_URL}}: final URL of the audited page
_placeholders.{{BRAND_NAME}}: brand name, from JSON-LD name, og:site_name, or the title's first segment
_placeholders.{{LOGO_URL}}: logo URL from JSON-LD logo or og:image
_placeholders.{{SAMEAS_LINKS}}: profile URLs already linked from the page, as JSON array items
_placeholders._rule: A placeholder is substituted ONLY when the value was observed on the page. Anything unobserved stays literal and is reported in placeholders_remaining. Never invent a business fact.
_placeholders.{{SAMEAS_LINKS_LEADING}}: same as SAMEAS_LINKS, but every entry carries a trailing comma; use when another array element follows it, so the pasted JSON still parses

access.http_ok.validation: Run `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" {{SITE_URL}}` and confirm it prints 200. A 3xx is acceptable only if the final hop is 200.
access.http_ok.target: your web server or hosting configuration — not the page markup

access.ai_crawlers_allowed.snippet:
# robots.txt at https://{{SITE_HOST}}/robots.txt
# Allow the crawlers that feed AI answer engines. Each needs its own group:
# a User-agent line only applies to the group it heads.

User-agent: GPTBot
Allow: /

User-agent: OAI-SearchBot
Allow: /

User-agent: ClaudeBot
Allow: /

User-agent: PerplexityBot
Allow: /

User-agent: Google-Extended
Allow: /

User-agent: CCBot
Allow: /

# Keep any existing rules for other crawlers below this point unchanged.
access.ai_crawlers_allowed.validation: Fetch https://{{SITE_HOST}}/robots.txt and confirm each bot has its own User-agent group with an Allow rule, and that no earlier `User-agent: *` group contains a `Disallow: /` that these groups fail to override.

access.indexable.snippet:
<!-- In <head>. Remove any noindex; state indexability explicitly. -->
<meta name="robots" content="index, follow">

<!-- If the block came from a header instead, remove or correct it server-side: -->
<!-- X-Robots-Tag: index, follow -->
access.indexable.validation: Run `curl -sSI {{SITE_URL}} | grep -i x-robots-tag` and confirm no `noindex` is returned, then view source and confirm no `<meta name="robots">` contains `noindex`.
access.indexable.target: the robots meta tag in <head>, or the X-Robots-Tag response header

render.content_without_js.validation: Run `curl -sS {{SITE_URL}} | grep -c "<h1"` and then search the same output for a sentence of your main copy. If the raw HTML does not already contain the text a reader sees, server-side rendering or prerendering is the fix — no markup change reproduces it.
render.content_without_js.target: your rendering setup (server-side rendering or prerendering) — not the markup

extraction.semantic_html.snippet:
… site identity and navigation …

{{PAGE_TITLE}}

… your primary content …
… contact and legal …
extraction.semantic_html.validation: View source and confirm exactly one `<main>` exists and your primary content sits inside it. Extraction tools use `<main>` to separate content from chrome.

extraction.facts_not_image_only.validation: Run `curl -sS {{SITE_URL}} | grep -F "<figcaption"` and confirm the numbers shown in the image appear as text. Copy the page into a plain-text editor: any fact that disappears is still invisible to an answer engine.
extraction.facts_not_image_only.target: each carrying a figure, and the text around it

content.title_descriptive.snippet:
<!-- In <head>. Name the thing, then what it is — not a bare brand token. -->
<title>{{BRAND_NAME}} — {{WHAT_YOU_DO}}</title>
content.title_descriptive.validation: Confirm the rendered `<title>` is between 15 and 70 characters and names both the brand and what it does. Search your own brand name and check the result headline reads as a description, not a label.

content.meta_description.snippet:
<!-- In <head>. One self-contained sentence stating what this page offers. -->
<meta name="description" content="{{ONE_SENTENCE_DESCRIPTION}}">
content.meta_description.validation: View source and confirm a single `<meta name="description">` of 50 to 160 characters. Paste the URL into a link-preview tool and confirm the description shown is yours, not text the platform guessed.

content.heading_hierarchy.snippet:
{{PAGE_TITLE}}

First major section

Detail within it

Second major section
content.heading_hierarchy.validation: List the headings in order and confirm there is exactly one `<h1>` and no level is skipped. Any outline tool or `document.querySelectorAll('h1,h2,h3,h4')` in the console will show the sequence.
content.heading_hierarchy.target: the heading elements in <body>, in document order

content.scannable_blocks.snippet:
<!-- Definition lists and tables are extracted far more reliably than the same facts in prose. -->
<dl>
  <dt>{{FACT_LABEL}}</dt><dd>{{FACT_VALUE}}</dd>
  <dt>{{FACT_LABEL_2}}</dt><dd>{{FACT_VALUE_2}}</dd>
</dl>
content.scannable_blocks.validation: Confirm the page contains at least one `<ul>`, `<ol>`, `<dl>` or `<table>` carrying real facts rather than navigation links, with two or more items in it.
content.scannable_blocks.target: the paragraphs holding your key facts

quotability.self_contained_facts.snippet: {{BRAND_NAME}} has served {{PLACE}} since {{YEAR}}.
quotability.self_contained_facts.validation: Take any three key sentences out of the page and read them cold. If a sentence needs the one before it to make sense, an answer engine will drop it rather than cite it.
quotability.self_contained_facts.target: the sentences stating your key claims

density.factual_ratio.validation: Count the sentences in your main content that contain a concrete number, name, date or specification. If fewer than a quarter do, the page is mostly framing and a summariser will condense away the part you wanted cited.

entity.structured_data_present.snippet:
<!-- In <head> or at the end of <body>. JSON-LD is the format answer engines read most reliably. -->
<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Organization",
  "name": "{{BRAND_NAME}}",
  "url": "{{SITE_URL}}",
  "logo": "{{LOGO_URL}}"
}
</script>
entity.structured_data_present.validation: Paste the URL into Google's Rich Results Test or schema.org's validator and confirm an Organization is detected with no errors.

entity.organization_declared.snippet:
<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Organization",
  "name": "{{BRAND_NAME}}",
  "url": "{{SITE_URL}}",
  "logo": "{{LOGO_URL}}",
  "description": "{{META_DESCRIPTION}}"
}
</script>

<!-- Use a more specific @type if one fits — Dentist, Bakery, LocalBusiness, SoftwareApplication.
     A specific type carries more meaning than the generic one, and any schema.org subtype counts. -->
entity.organization_declared.validation: Run the Rich Results Test and confirm the detected entity's name matches the brand name a visitor sees in your header. A mismatch is worse than no markup: it tells the machine you are a different organisation.
entity.organization_declared.target: the Organization node in your JSON-LD

entity.sameas_present.snippet: {{BRAND_NAME}} on {{PLATFORM}}
entity.sameas_present.validation: Confirm every URL in `sameAs` loads and is a profile you control. A dead or wrong link weakens corroboration instead of strengthening it.
entity.sameas_present.target: the sameAs array on your Organization node

entity.sameas_authority.snippet:
<!-- Add at least one record somebody else maintains. Any ONE of these anchors your identity;
     a local business does not need Wikidata, and a directory listing works just as well. -->
"sameAs": [
{{SAMEAS_LINKS_LEADING}}
    "{{AUTHORITY_PROFILE_URL}}"
]
entity.sameas_authority.validation: Confirm at least one `sameAs` target is a record you do not publish yourself — a Google Business Profile, an industry directory, a companies registry or a review platform. Links only to your own accounts cannot settle which business you are.
entity.sameas_authority.target: the sameAs array on your Organization node

entity.opengraph_identity.snippet:
<!-- In <head>. Open Graph drives social previews; it is not a substitute for schema.org,
     but a missing og:site_name loses the identity signal on every shared link. -->
<meta property="og:site_name" content="{{BRAND_NAME}}">
<meta property="og:title" content="{{PAGE_TITLE}}">
<meta property="og:url" content="{{SITE_URL}}">
<meta property="og:type" content="website">
<meta property="og:image" content="{{LOGO_URL}}">
entity.opengraph_identity.validation: Paste the URL into any link-preview debugger and confirm the site name and title shown are the ones you intend.
entity.opengraph_identity.target: the Open Graph meta tags in <head>

entity.name_consistency.snippet:
<!-- The same brand string in all three places. A machine treats a difference as a different
     organisation, which is exactly the mistaken-identity failure this category measures. -->
<title>{{BRAND_NAME}} — …</title>
<meta property="og:site_name" content="{{BRAND_NAME}}">
<!-- and in JSON-LD: -->  "name": "{{BRAND_NAME}}"
entity.name_consistency.validation: Compare the `name` in your JSON-LD, the `og:site_name`, and the brand shown in your header. A tagline appended after a separator is fine; a genuinely different name is not.
entity.name_consistency.target: the <title>, the og:site_name tag and the JSON-LD name — all three

orientation.heading_first_viewport.snippet:
{{HEADLINE}}

{{SUPPORTING_SENTENCE}}
orientation.heading_first_viewport.validation: Load the page at 1280x800 and confirm a real heading is visible without scrolling. A visitor arriving from an AI citation decides in that first screen whether they reached the right place.

orientation.primary_cta.snippet: {{CTA_LABEL}}
orientation.primary_cta.validation: Load the page without scrolling and confirm one obvious next step is visible, and that it is an `<a>` or `<button>` element rather than a styled `<div>`.
orientation.primary_cta.target: the first screen, above the fold

orientation.content_not_obstructed.snippet:
<!-- Constrain a persistent banner so it cannot cover the first screen. -->
.consent-banner, .promo-bar {
  position: sticky;      /* not fixed, so it scrolls out of the way */
  max-height: 20vh;      /* never more than a fifth of the viewport */
}
orientation.content_not_obstructed.validation: Load the page in a clean browser profile at 1280x800 and confirm no overlay covers more than about a fifth of the first screen before any interaction.
orientation.content_not_obstructed.target: the CSS for your banner or overlay

orientation.viewport_meta.snippet:
<!-- In <head>. Without it, mobile browsers render at desktop width and zoom out. -->
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
orientation.viewport_meta.validation: Open the page on a phone, or in device emulation, and confirm the text is readable without pinch-zooming.

orientation.value_proposition.snippet:
{{WHAT_YOU_DO}}

{{WHO_IT_IS_FOR_AND_WHY_IT_IS_DIFFERENT}}
orientation.value_proposition.validation: Show the first screen to someone who does not know the company and ask what you sell and to whom. If they cannot say, an AI-referred visitor will not stay to find out.
orientation.value_proposition.target: the headline and the first paragraph under it

orientation.legibility.snippet:
/* Body text below about 14px drives away visitors who arrived on a phone. */
body { font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.5; }
orientation.legibility.validation: Inspect a body paragraph and confirm the computed `font-size` is at least 14px, ideally 16px.
orientation.legibility.target: the CSS rule setting the body font size
